beats.label: S1 · The cave takes Mikkel
beats.text: Mikkel Nielsen vanishes from a cave near Winden's nuclear plant during a group search for a missing dealer. A boy's corpse in 1980s clothes surfaces the next day — not Mikkel.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The inciting event that pulls every family into the cave and every era into each other.

beats.label: S1 · Winden repeats itself
beats.text: Officer Ulrich Nielsen leads the case, haunted by his brother Mads' 1986 disappearance. Dead birds, ruptured eardrums, and a locked cave door tie both eras to the plant.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the 33-year pattern that every later season builds on.

beats.label: S1 · Mikkel becomes Michael
beats.text: Mikkel wakes in 1986 and is taken in by the young nurse Ines. He grows up as Michael Kahnwald, marries Hannah, fathers Jonas, and kills himself decades later in 2019.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The loop that makes Jonas his own uncle and defines every future stake.

beats.label: S1 · Sic mundus creatus est
beats.text: A stranger delivers Michael's suicide letter to Jonas: his father was Mikkel. Jonas enters a cave passage marked 'Sic mundus creatus est' and steps out into 1986.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Jonas crosses time for the first time — the transition from mystery show to time-travel story.

beats.label: S1 · Ulrich to 1953
beats.text: Ulrich chases Helge Doppler through the passage to 1953, where he beats nine-year-old Helge nearly to death in a bunker to stop the killings. He is arrested and left there.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Ulrich from the present for the rest of the series and shows the loop cannot be broken by murder.

beats.label: S1 · Noah's machine
beats.text: The priest Noah is using abducted children — Erik, Yasin, and eventually Mads — as test subjects in a chair-mounted device meant to build a working time portal under Helge's cabin.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the antagonist behind the abductions and the goal — a stable portal — that drives the next season.

beats.label: S1 · Jonas is his own future
beats.text: The Stranger reveals himself as an adult Jonas, sent to destroy the wormhole with Tannhaus' brass machine. As it activates, young Jonas is hurled into a post-apocalyptic Winden of 2052.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the future-Jonas / present-Jonas split that structures all of season 2.

cliffhanger.text: Jonas has been thrown 33 years into a ruined future Winden, Mikkel is trapped as Michael in the past, and Ulrich is locked up in 1953. The wormhole under the town is real, and every attempt to shut it has fed it.
questions: Who is really directing Noah and the abductions?
Can Jonas ever get back — and if he does, does he unmake himself?

characters.name: Jonas Kahnwald
characters.line: Teenage protagonist, stranded in a post-apocalyptic 2052 after his older self triggered the wormhole he was trying to destroy.

characters.name: Mikkel Nielsen / Michael Kahnwald
characters.line: The missing boy, now revealed as the man who grew up in the 1980s to become Jonas' father and later kill himself.
characters.note: One person, two names in two eras.

characters.name: Ulrich Nielsen
characters.line: Winden police officer who followed the passage to 1953 and is now jailed there for beating a child Helge.

characters.name: The Stranger
characters.line: An adult Jonas from the future, working to collapse the wormhole and prevent his own loop.

characters.name: Noah
characters.line: The priest running the child-killing time-machine experiments, taking orders from a larger organisation Winden has not yet seen.

characters.name: Charlotte Doppler
characters.line: Winden's police chief, the only local closing in on the cave-plant-1986 connection.

beats.label: S2 · Six days to the apocalypse
beats.text: Six days out from 27 June 2020, disappearances have mounted and federal investigator Clausen has arrived. Time travel is now openly discussed among Winden's adults.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the season's countdown and moves the story from secret to shared knowledge.

beats.label: S2 · Adam is Jonas
beats.text: In 1921, a disfigured elder called Adam — an even older Jonas — leads a society named Sic Mundus and directs Noah to prepare for the coming apocalypse.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the season's antagonist and reveals Jonas' own future as the man engineering the loop.

beats.label: S2 · The God Particle
beats.text: Trapped in 2053, Jonas finds a survivor colony led by an adult Elisabeth Doppler. He learns of a floating black mass called the God Particle that can be used as a portable portal.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the mechanism that lets characters travel anywhere in time, replacing the fixed cave passage.

beats.label: S2 · Michael must die
beats.text: Jonas travels back to stop his father Michael's suicide. Michael and an elderly Claudia convince him it must happen — without it, Mikkel is never sent back and Jonas is never born.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Locks in the fatalism of the loop and turns Jonas from disrupter into reluctant caretaker.

beats.label: S2 · Charlotte's parentage
beats.text: Noah reveals to Charlotte that she is his daughter, raised by Tannhaus after two strangers left her with him. Her mother's identity is still withheld from her and from the audience.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the Winden family tree as its own puzzle, the piece the next season pulls on hardest.

beats.label: S2 · Winden burns
beats.text: Clausen forces open the drums of radioactive waste Aleksander secretly buried at the plant, triggering the apocalypse. Katharina opens the cave gate as the town is razed.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The predicted disaster arrives — the ruined 2052 Jonas has seen is now the shared present.

beats.label: S2 · Another world
beats.text: Adam shoots Martha dead moments before the apocalypse. Another Martha then appears from a parallel reality and pulls Jonas through — into a world where he was never born.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Breaks the show open from one timeline to two entangled ones, the whole subject of season 3.

cliffhanger.text: Winden has been destroyed on schedule and Adam has murdered Martha to break the cycle. But a second Martha, from a parallel reality, has appeared to pull Jonas out — the story now has two worlds to close, not one.
questions: Is Adam's Martha permanently dead, or does death loop too?
What are the rules of this second world, and where does Jonas fit if he was never born there?
Who is running things on the other side, if Adam runs this one?

characters.name: Jonas Kahnwald
characters.line: Just pulled through by an alternate Martha into a parallel reality, the Winden he knows now destroyed behind him.

characters.name: Adam
characters.line: The disfigured elder Jonas who runs Sic Mundus from 1921 and has just killed his younger love to try to end the cycle.

characters.name: Claudia Tiedemann
characters.line: The veteran time traveller openly guiding young Jonas against Adam, with her own long game underway.

characters.name: Martha Nielsen
characters.line: Shot dead by Adam in Jonas' world — while a version of her from another reality has just stepped into her place.

characters.name: Charlotte Doppler
characters.line: Now knows Noah is her father and Tannhaus only raised her, but does not know who her mother is.

characters.name: Katharina Nielsen
characters.line: Convinced of time travel and going after her son — has just opened the cave gate as Winden burns.

beats.label: S3 · A world without Jonas
beats.text: Jonas emerges in a Winden where he was never born. Ulrich divorced Katharina and married Hannah, Franziska is the deaf sister instead of Elisabeth, and Martha does not know him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the mirror world's terms and makes Jonas a stranger in his own story.

beats.label: S3 · Eva against Adam
beats.text: An elder Martha — 'Eva' — leads Erit Lux, this world's counterpart to Sic Mundus. She and Adam are locked in a knot: he wants both worlds erased, she wants both preserved.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the season's opposing forces and reframes the fight as two worlds, not two people.

beats.label: S3 · The Unknown is theirs
beats.text: Martha is pregnant by Jonas. Their child — a traveller who appears as boy, man, and elder at once, called the Unknown — is revealed as the root of the Winden family tree itself.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names Jonas and Martha as the origin of the loop the whole show has been unwinding.

beats.label: S3 · Two Marthas, two Jonases
beats.text: In Eva's world an alternate Martha shoots Jonas dead; in another branch a Martha rescues him from Adam's apocalypse. Both branches coexist, entangled at the moment of her death.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The physical bridge between the two worlds — Martha's death is where they meet.

beats.label: S3 · A third world
beats.text: Claudia — who killed and replaced her Eva-world counterpart to spy on both sides — cracks the truth: a third, 'origin' world exists outside Adam's and Eva's, and the loop began there.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reframes the whole series: neither Adam's nor Eva's world is real, both are shards of another.

beats.label: S3 · Tannhaus built it
beats.text: H.G. Tannhaus, grieving his son's family killed in a car crash, built a time machine to bring them back. The attempt shattered the origin world into Adam's and Eva's.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The cause of everything — a single act of private grief, not a conspiracy.

beats.label: S3 · Undo
beats.text: Jonas and Martha travel to the origin world and stop Tannhaus' family from dying in the crash. The time machine is never built; Adam's and Eva's worlds — and both of them — cease to exist.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The resolution: closing the loop erases everyone born from it, including the protagonists.

cliffhanger.text: Only characters whose existence did not depend on the loop remain, in a Winden with no time travel. At a dinner party a pregnant Hannah notices a yellow raincoat and feels a passing déjà vu, then says she has always liked the name Jonas.
questions: Do echoes of the vanished worlds still linger in the survivors?
Is the origin world truly free of the cycle, or only quieter?
What kind of Jonas will Hannah's child grow up to be?

characters.name: Jonas Kahnwald
characters.line: Erased along with Adam's and Eva's worlds after undoing the origin — the version of him that ever existed no longer does.

characters.name: Martha Nielsen
characters.line: Erased with Jonas after saving Tannhaus' family — the two of them the last casualties of the loop they were born from.

characters.name: Adam
characters.line: The elder Jonas who spent lifetimes trying to end the cycle; accepts the true fix and vanishes with his world.

characters.name: Eva
characters.line: The elder Martha of the mirror world, Adam's counterpart; embraces him at the end as their shared existence is undone.

characters.name: Claudia Tiedemann
characters.line: The traveller who found the third world and handed Adam the answer that ends both his and Eva's realities.

characters.name: Hannah
characters.line: A survivor in the origin world, pregnant with a new Jonas by a healed Torben Wöller, faintly haunted by something she cannot name.
